tex_content.html:
Definition
1. ch5:compact\group chapter-5 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0087, page-0088

A map $T:\V _1\to \V _2$ is compact if it maps bounded sets to relatively compact sets, equivalently, if every image of a bounded sequence has a convergent subsequence. A compact linear map is continuous.
